POST and PUT data support

Configurable verbosity levels

Fleet: Centralized agent management for data collection
Lake: Elastic, high-performance data storage powered by InstaStore™ technology

Never Block, Never Drop architecture for data reliability

Advanced visualizations (e.g., box plots, heatmaps, bubble charts, Sankey diagrams)
Real User Monitoring (RUM) and SLO management dashboards

artillery.about: Artillery is a modern, powerful, and easy-to-use performance and reliability testing toolkit designed to ship scalable applications that remain performant under load. It supports full-stack testing, including load testing, scalable Playwright E2E testing, and production monitoring in one toolkit. It is designed to be incrementally adoptable and uses a "batteries-included" philosophy to prioritize developer experience.
features: Distributed load testing with zero infrastructure management required
Built-in support for HTTP, WebSocket, and Socket.io protocols
Plugin system for additional protocol support (e.g., HLS, Kinesis, Kafka)
Supports running tests on AWS (Lambda/Fargate) or Azure (ACI) directly from user accounts
Automatic metric aggregation and cost reporting for tests
Support for complex test scenarios using TypeScript/JavaScript
artillery.pricing: Artillery offers a free Developer plan ($0/month), a Team plan ($199/month), and a Scale plan ($499/month). Enterprise add-ons are available starting at $1199/month. Annual subscription options offer a 20% savings. Subscriptions are also available via AWS Marketplace.
aiFeatures: Can be integrated with coding agents
Supports no-code test generation via Playwright codegen
Enables reuse of existing Playwright test suites for load testing with automatic Core Web Vitals capture

latestRelease.notes: The Artillery changelog tracks feature updates and improvements for Artillery CLI and Artillery Cloud, including updates to the HTTP engine, Playwright integration, AWS Fargate/Lambda support, Slack plugin, and reporting dashboard enhancements. It integrates with the Artillery CLI to offer test observability, real-time reporting, collaboration tools, and CI/CD integrations for testing suites including Playwright.
features: Centralized dashboard for test reports
Real-time test monitoring and streaming
Support for Playwright end-to-end and load testing
Distributed load testing (AWS & Azure)
CI/CD integration (e.g., GitHub Actions PR comments)
Synthetic monitoring
Test observability with custom charts and visualizations
Team collaboration tools, including test sharing and commenting
artillery-cloud.pricing: Artillery Cloud offers a free tier for hobby and proof-of-concept projects. Paid plans include a Team plan at $199/month and a Business/Scale plan at $499/month. Enterprise add-ons start at $1,199/month. Subscriptions are available via the Artillery website or AWS Marketplace. Annual billing options are available for a 20% discount.

latestRelease.notes: The latest version is Artillery v2.0.33. Recent updates include upgrades to Playwright v1.60.0 support, various core fixes for timeouts and module loading, improvements to AWS ECS/Fargate reliability, and Artillery Cloud specific fixes for trace upload errors.

aws-distributed-load-testing.about: Distributed Load Testing on AWS is an open-source solution that automates performance testing at scale, allowing users to simulate hundreds to millions of concurrent users against any endpoint in any AWS Region without provisioning servers. It is designed to identify performance bottlenecks and system behavior under load throughout the application lifecycle.

Distributed test runner management across multiple AWS Regions using Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate
Web console, CLI, and headless deployment options
Live data visualization and automated performance analytics
Timezone-aware scheduling and tagging for test scenarios
Downloadable test results and comparison against baselines

azure-load-testing.about: Azure Load Testing (now part of Azure App Testing) is a fully managed load-testing service by Microsoft that enables developers, testers, and QA engineers to generate high-scale load and identify performance bottlenecks in applications. The service allows for simulations of traffic for applications hosted on Azure or in other environments, including multicloud, on-premises, or hybrid setups. It abstracts infrastructure management, enabling users to create tests via URL configuration or by using existing scripts (Apache JMeter, Locust, or Playwright).
features: Fully managed, cloud-scale infrastructure with no setup required.
Support for Apache JMeter, Locust, and Playwright scripts.
URL-based performance testing for web applications and REST APIs.
Detailed resource metrics collection for performance bottleneck identification.
Continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline integration.
Support for various protocols including HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, JDBC, FTP, and LDAP (via JMeter).
Automated networking configuration for public and private endpoints.
Ability to define test failure criteria and parameterize load tests.
azure-load-testing.pricing: Azure Load Testing follows a pay-as-you-go model based on Virtual User Hour (VUH) consumption, with no monthly resource fees. Consumption beyond 10,000 VUH is priced at $0.06 per VUH. Users only pay for the VUH consumed during test runs. Minimum VUH per test run applies.
aiFeatures: Automated issue detection and root cause identification using AI.
Natural language interaction for test generation and analysis within Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot, and the Azure platform.
AI-driven workflows to simplify testing processes.

latestRelease.version: v1.2.2 (GitHub Action for Azure Load Testing)
latestRelease.notes: The latest release (as of June 2026) for the Azure Load Testing GitHub Action introduced a parameter to ignore the wait for test run completion, allowing users to trigger test runs in workflows without blocking until completion.

bombardier.about: Bombardier is a fast, cross-platform HTTP(S) benchmarking and load-testing tool written in the Go programming language. It is designed to flood web servers with requests to test their performance and can simulate multiple concurrent users. It utilizes the fasthttp library by default for high performance, though it also supports the standard net/http library for specific requirements like HTTP/2.x.
features: High-performance HTTP(S) benchmarking
Cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows) support
Supports both fasthttp and standard net/http clients
Customizable concurrency levels and test duration
Supports HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 testing
Detailed performance statistics (QPS, latency, throughput)
Configurable output formats via user-defined templates

Cloud Insights for automated performance issue surfacing

CI/CD integration for continuous performance testing
